The right person is a player-coach who can still build a defensible model personally, but whose greatest impact comes from raising the capability and output of the team around them. jobs.title: Deployed Strategist
jobs.description_text: Job: You will own customer outcomes across Parallel's strategic accounts and make retention and expansion a deliberate motion as we scale. You'll define what success looks like with our customers before go-live and build the dashboard tying every metric back to the economic case the GTM team sold against. You'll partner with Deployed Engineering on strategic deployments, build reference architectures for the workloads the customer base is concentrating around, and run a structured operating cadence that turns realized ROI into expansion, renewals, and references the AE team carries into the next deal. You'll also own the customer → product feedback loop, routing usage signals and friction patterns into prioritized input Product can act on. You: Have run post-sale at an infrastructure or AI company and can speak credibly about agent frameworks, background-agent workloads, and how our APIs compose into a real customer workflow. You've defined outcome metrics tied to commercial impact before, and you know the difference between a customer who's using the product and a customer whose ROI is visible enough to expand against. You see expansion whitespace early, you know when a renewal is at risk before the QBR, and you're energized by building the function from scratch rather than inheriting one.

jobs.title: GTM Recruiter
jobs.description_text: Job: You will own full-cycle recruiting for sales at Parallel, running searches from intake through close. You'll partner directly with hiring managers and founders to define role scope, build interview loops, and calibrate what "great" looks like for each role. You'll drive sourcing and outbound for hard-to-fill and senior roles, manage candidates through the pipeline without letting anyone go cold, and help sharpen the scorecards and playbooks the team runs on as headcount scales fast. You'll report on pipeline health and hiring velocity to the recruiting lead, and you'll be trusted to close high-conviction offers on your own. You: Have run full-cycle sales recruiting at an early-stage or fast-growing company and know how to own searches end to end. You can hire AEs in your sleep. You've worked sales and marketing roles and know how to flex your pitch and interview process for each. You write outbound that gets responses from people who aren't looking, and you know how to close a candidate who has three other offers. You work well solo but you're just as sharp coordinating with other recruiters on shared priorities, and you move fast because slow hiring kills momentum at a company this stage.

jobs.title: Product Marketing, Ecosystem Partners
jobs.description_text: Job: You will make Parallel the default web layer for developers and enterprises building AI agents on our partners’ platforms. You’ll own positioning and messaging across our cloud, developer-tool, agent-framework, and services partners: what each integration does, who it’s for, and why it matters. You’ll run joint launches end to end, from narrative and code examples to launch content and the follow-through that turns a launch into adoption. You’ll build enablement that partners’ sales and solutions teams actually use, decide with partnerships, product, and sales which integrations get priority, and own the adoption and pipeline they drive. What you hear from partners and the developers building on them goes straight back into the roadmap. You: Have done partner, ecosystem, or integrations product marketing at an API, infrastructure, or developer-tools company, and can show what a platform launch moved. You’re technical enough to write a code-backed launch post and credible with the engineers who read it. You can write a one-pager that sells, and you can tell a real differentiator from fluff. Experience with cloud marketplaces or open-source agent frameworks is a real advantage. You’d rather ship, learn, and say what you got wrong than polish a deck.

jobs.title: Design Engineer
jobs.description_text: Job: We’re hiring a design engineer to help shape and build interactive experiences across Parallel’s website, product, and special projects. The work ranges from refining everyday interactions and motion to creating visual essays, data visualizations, launch pages, and minisites. You’ll work alongside designers, marketers, and engineers from the first rough idea through to production. That means prototyping possible directions, contributing to our core website, and getting the details right in the browser. You’ll also build reusable components and patterns that help us ship the next project faster. You: You’re a design engineer or a frontend engineer with strong design instincts. Your work shows care for typography, layout, and the timing and feel of an interaction. You’ve shipped working websites and can point to the decisions you made along the way. You’re comfortable with modern frontend and animation libraries, and know when to build something custom. You move quickly in prototypes and carry that work through to a responsive, accessible, performant site. About Parallel Design: We design for a web used by both people and agents, grounding our work in real code, data, and evidence. We draw from the history of the web, computing, and publishing to help explain what comes next, while leaving room for experiments, tangents, and things made simply because they’re good.

jobs.title: Accounting Manager
jobs.description_text: Job: You will own accounting at Parallel end to end, from month-end close and financial reporting to technical accounting, audits, tax, and statutory compliance. You'll manage multi-entity accounting as Parallel scales internationally, own our relationships with external accounting, tax, and audit partners, and drive the systems and future ERP decisions that support a fast-growing business. You'll partner closely with revenue leadership and the finance lead on quote-to-cash improvements and billing operations, and you'll build the processes and infrastructure that let the accounting function scale without breaking. You: Have 8+ years of accounting experience at a high-growth technology company, with a track record of taking on increasing ownership of the function. You have deep expertise in US GAAP, technical accounting, and SaaS revenue recognition, and you're comfortable with multi-entity and international operations, transfer pricing, and inter-company accounting. You understand billing systems and revenue operations well enough to partner directly with commercial teams, not just report on them after the fact. You're a builder who wants to design the systems, not just operate them, and you stay close to the details even as you take on more scope. Bonus if you've led an ERP migration or can write SQL to answer your own questions instead of waiting on someone else's dashboard.

jobs.title: Strategic Finance
jobs.description_text: Job: You will help shape Parallel’s business and financial strategy as a member of the Strategic Finance team. You’ll partner with leaders across the company, own key financial models, and use your analysis to drive critical company decisions. Projects may span compute analysis, pricing and packaging, unit economics by product, strategic distribution partnerships, and setting up KPIs for the business. You’ll pull data from wherever it lives and set it up for ongoing reporting to the leadership team. Your scope will grow as fast as you earn it. You: You’ve spent a few years in a high-rigor seat like investment banking or strategy consulting, followed by an investing role at a private equity or growth firm, or a finance role at a high-growth company. You’ve built detailed, complex models from first principles, and you can defend every assumption when someone pushes back. You’ve used AI tools to do real work faster, and you’re eager to find new ways to apply them. You take ownership without being asked, flag problems early, and want to grow into a finance and general business leader at Parallel.

jobs.title: Brand Designer
jobs.description_text: Job: We’re hiring a senior brand designer who’s a generalist first, with a particular strength in technical storytelling and information design. You’ll help explain a deeply technical product to a wider audience, and apply and extend our brand system across the work we put into the world. You’ll be part of the design team, working closely with technical marketing and DevRel to shape the story from the first outline. The work includes diagrams, benchmark and eval visualizations, docs and API illustrations, and visual essays like The Web as Ground Truth https://parallel.ai/the-web-as-ground-truth. You’ll also work across launch pages, blog art direction, conference and keynote graphics, motion, and social. You: Your portfolio shows strong typography, composition, and range across brand, web, and motion. You can learn a complex subject, find the idea that matters, and explain it at different levels of depth. You bring ideas to the narrative and are comfortable working through them in prototypes and motion. Experience with developer or technical products is a plus, as is a strong writing instinct. jobs.title: Research Scientist - Post-Training
jobs.description_text: Pluralis Research works on Protocol Learning: training and serving large models in a fully decentralized way on small consumer-grade devices connected via the internet. Despite being dismissed as infeasible, we have made significant advances on this problem, most recently Agora, a permissionless run that pretrained an 8B model from scratch on consumer GPUs spread over the internet, with no single participant ever holding the full weights (tech report https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13332). While many of the core research problems have been solved, Protocol Learning unlocks a series of new challenges. For the mission in full, read A Third Path: Protocol Learning https://pluralis.ai/blog/a-third-path-protocol-learning/. Agora gave us a pretrained 8B model. Post-training is how we make it useful for agentic use-cases. But every post-training stack you've seen assumes a datacenter — synchronous rollouts, fast interconnects, trusted workers. Ours gets none of that. It has to run on consumer GPUs, and Macs spread across the public internet, training a model whose weights no single participant ever holds, with rollouts arriving from a geo-distributed inference pipeline at high latencies. Your primary role is to make RL post-training work here anyway — the algorithms and the system, end-to-end. For the mission in full, read A Third Path: Protocol Learning https://pluralis.ai/blog/a-third-path-protocol-learning/. Our training and inference network is trustless, and the workers are GPUs scattered across the world. Many things can go wrong in this system.
